messages:
max: tagging eng-runtime + eng-ml + product — we have three enterprise customers pushing for an 'Optimize Toolkit' delivery: automated batching heuristics, prefix/KV caching recommendations, and quantization guidance. Need to nail PRD scope and launch criteria. Who can help sketch acceptance criteria + rollout plan?

raj: high-level Q: are customers asking for prescriptive auto-applies, or for a recommendations-only workflow they can opt into? that determines infra risk. for MVP i suggest recommendations + SDK hooks, not auto-apply.

carmen: +1 on recommendations-only for M1. platform ops wants minimal control-plane surface area — prefer a rules engine that outputs URLs/SDK payloads we can consume. also need telemetry hooks to attribute savings.

ian: runtime caveats: KV cache invalidation, per-tenant memory budgets, and multi-model pipelines (e.g., reranker -> generator). streaming/token-by-token cases must not break with batching. list of edge cases we should enumerate: 1) streaming + batching mixing, 2) cache staleness + model updates, 3) quantization fallback when output quality drops.

elaine: from CS/customer signals: acceptance must include quality/regression gates. propose these concrete gates: - latency regression <= 10% P95 vs baseline for latency-sensitive endpoints; - cost reduction >= 20% for batch-heavy workloads (as measured by token-cost per 1M tokens); - no more than 1% increase in hallucination rate on eval prompt set. also docs + migration guide required for customers.

raj: sketching a PRD checklist / rollout plan: RFC -> prototype -> internal canary (select customers) -> metric gates -> gradual rollout. metric gate example we can use in canary: ```
{
  "gate": "p95_latency",
  "threshold": 1.10, // 10% allowed regression
  "baseline_period": "14d",
  "monitoring_window": "1h",
  "action": "rollback"
}
```

carmen: API shape question: do we expose a unified /optimize/recommendation endpoint that returns batching/cache/quant advice, or separate endpoints per recommendation type? unified is easier for UI but harder for incremental rollout. thoughts?

max: propose a scope split: M1 (recommendations engine + minimal SDK + UI for suggestions + PRD with acceptance criteria and canary flow), M2 (auto-apply policies, infra autoscale integration, and ML-driven adaptive batching). owners: raj (ML heuristics), ian (runtime), carmen (platform), elaine (customer docs). ETA: aim for M1 RFC + prototype in 6 weeks, canary in 12.

ian: i'll own runtime changes for M1 prototype; immediate items to spec in the RFC: eviction semantics for KV cache, per-tenant memory limits, behavior during model version switches, and a test plan (unit + perf + canary suites). add quantization edge tests: detuning thresholds, fallback to FP, and metricized output-quality checks.

elaine: i'll draft the customer-facing migration doc and a short FAQ for common edge cases (model rollouts, jitter during canary). happy to co-author the acceptance criteria appendix.

deploy-bot: Created RFC draft at https://docs.internal.redwood/optkit/rfc-1719234567 (edit permissions: eng-ml, eng-runtime, product).

max: excellent. next steps: raj + ian + carmen to draft RFC sections this week, elaine to start docs, and we sync next Tue 10am. ping me if blockers.
